messages:
maria_sales: Heads-up: SentinelBank wants a Private Deploy POC. Their infra constraints: no internet egress except an allowlist (three hostnames), must preserve client src IP for security logs, and they require KMS/BYOK details for the questionnaire. They also asked for an upfront POC vs reserved pricing estimate. Can we assemble a short network playbook + firewall snippets to send to their net team?

chet_netops: Two main architectures to propose: 1) Cross-account VPC peering (best for srcIP preservation, minimal app changes). 2) Interface PrivateLink endpoints (simpler isolation, but note our egress from ENIs will SNAT so srcIP won't be preserved). If they can't accept SNAT, peering is the route.

lia_solutions: For customers reluctant to peer, propose a proxy approach that injects X-Forwarded-For (requires app change). Also mention option: place a small customer-side TCP proxy (nginx/haproxy) that logs original IP and forwards to our endpoint.

omar_security: For the security questionnaire: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (cross-account grant pattern). Enterprise can request HSM-backed keys. Key rotation controlled by customer KMS policy; we do not retain plaintext inputs beyond processing unless explicitly enabled for analytics. I'll prepare definitive language.

ben_infra: Practical firewall snippet for their ops team (they prefer examples they can paste):

# AWS SG egress (restrict to Redwood proxies and DNS)
Type: HTTPS  Protocol: TCP  Port Range: 443  Destination: 203.0.113.10/32, 203.0.113.11/32
Type: DNS    Protocol: UDP  Port Range: 53   Destination: 198.51.100.5/32

If they require hostname-based allowlist, recommend outbound HTTPS proxy with FQDN allowlist (we can provide stable proxy IPs for the POC). Example iptables to force-proxy pattern:

iptables -t nat -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.0.1.5:3128
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 203.0.113.10 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP

Note: For peering, ensure route table entries exist in both accounts and do not NAT traffic. If they use TGW, confirm route propagation and that the peering attachment is accepted in the correct account.

lia_solutions: Add a short checklist for their infra: allow DNS, NTP (UDP 123), healthcheck endpoints (TCP 443 to proxy IPs), and enable TCP MSS clamping if they have appliances that fragment MTU. Also call out certificate-pinning pitfalls if they have TLS inspection.

omar_security: TLS inspection will break pinned certs; recommend mTLS or disable inspection for Redwood endpoints. For KMS BYOK steps: customer creates CMK, grants our service principal encrypt/decrypt via cross-account grant, and we log usage. I'll attach the sample IAM policy.

bot_deploy: Ticket created: SALES-4712 - "SentinelBank POC network + KMS pack". Owner: chet_netops. Due: 48 hours.

maria_sales: Perfect. Action items: Chet produce the one-page network playbook (peering vs PrivateLink decision table + SG/iptables snippets) and a small diagram. Omar finalize KMS/HSM text for questionnaire. Ben draft the POC pricing rows (POC discount, reserved monthly commit). I'll attach to the RFP reply once ready. :thumbsup:

chet_netops: Will deliver playbook and diagrams by tomorrow EOD. I'll include example route table entries and an explicit note: "Peering preserves srcIP only if no NAT is applied on either side."

ben_infra: I'll prepare pricing examples for 30d POC, 90d discounted reserved, and 12mo committed reserved. Numbers are illustrative until Finance signs off.

maria_sales: Thanks team — I'll loop in the customer infra lead (sentinel-net) after we have the doc.
